questions.question: If a + b + c = 0 and a = 0.5, b = 0.3, c = -0.8, then what is the value of (a³ + b³ + c³) ÷ (abc)?
questions.questionHtml: If a + b + c = 0 and a = 0.5, b = 0.3, c = -0.8, then what is the value of (a³ + b³ + c³) ÷ (abc)?
questions.solution:
When a + b + c = 0,

a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

So,

(a³ + b³ + c³) ÷ (abc)
= 3abc ÷ abc
= 3

questions.question: In right triangle PQR, right-angled at Q, PQ = 12 cm. QS is a perpendicular drawn from Q to the hypotenuse PR. If the length of the hypotenuse PR is twice the length of the altitude QS, i.e. PR = 2QS, and ∠QPR = ∠QRP, find the numerical value of PR² + QS².
questions.questionHtml: In right triangle PQR, right-angled at Q, PQ = 12 cm. QS is a perpendicular drawn from Q to the hypotenuse PR. If the length of the hypotenuse PR is twice the length of the altitude QS, i.e. PR = 2QS, and ∠QPR = ∠QRP, find the numerical value of PR² + QS².
questions.solution:
∠QPR = ∠QRP, so opposite sides are equal.

PQ = QR = 12 cm

PR² = PQ² + QR²
PR² = 12² + 12²
PR² = 144 + 144 = 288

So, PR = 12√2

Given: PR = 2QS
12√2 = 2QS
QS = 6√2

Now,

PR² + QS² = (12√2)² + (6√2)²
= 288 + 72
= 360

questions.question: In triangle PQR, the incenter is located at point I. If the lengths of the sides are p, q, and r, which of the following statements is always true?
questions.questionHtml: In triangle PQR, the incenter is located at point I. If the lengths of the sides are p, q, and r, which of the following statements is always true?

options.text: Distance from I to vertex P is equal to distance from I to vertex Q.
options.html: Distance from I to vertex P is equal to distance from I to vertex Q.

options.text: Distance from I to side p is equal to distance from I to side q.
options.html: Distance from I to side p is equal to distance from I to side q.

options.text: Distance from I to vertex P is twice the distance from I to side p.
options.html: Distance from I to vertex P is twice the distance from I to side p.

options.text: Point I is always equidistant from the three vertices P, Q, and R.
options.html: Point I is always equidistant from the three vertices P, Q, and R.

questions.solution:
Incenter is the point where the angle bisectors of a triangle meet.

The incenter is always equidistant from all three sides of the triangle.

So, distance from I to side p = distance from I to side q = distance from I to side r.

Therefore, option (b) is correct.
